transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
President Trump was on the campaign trail yesterday predicting major Republican victories
at a rally in Dubuque, Iowa, and as Iowa Public Radio's Tom Barton says, his closing message
resonated with attendees.
Trump urged Iowans to vote Republican for lower taxes and bigger paychecks while portraying
Democrats as a threat to their livelihoods and safety.
"So a vote for any Democrat anywhere in the country is a vote to put a deranged group
of extremists into power and it could really hurt us."
Davenport resident Wade Martin says that message resonates with him.
He's voting for Republicans in tight races for U.S. Senate and Governor.
"They're both looking out for our best interests and I think if we just keep a Republican party
in office we're going to be in a good place."
Congresswoman Ashley Henson faces Democratic State Representative Josh Turek in a tight
race that could decide Senate control.
Meanwhile GOP businessman Zach Lane seeks to hold Iowa's governor's office against
a strong Democratic challenge by state auditor Rob Sand.
For NPR News, I'm Tom Barton in Dubuque, Iowa.
In Los Angeles, the retrial begins for the man accused of starting a fire that eventually
turned into the deadly 2025 Palisades fire.
Steve Futterman has more.
The prosecution claims Jonathan Rinderkinesh was angry and despondent when he allegedly
started the Lachman fire in the early hours of January 1 last year.
That fire, the prosecution says, smoldered for around a week before reigniting later
as the Palisades fire.
The defense has a much different view.
It says the Lachman fire was likely ignited by New Year's fireworks.
Former federal prosecutor Lori Levinson says in the original trial jurors nearly found
Rinderkinesh not guilty.
The jury hung, leaning 10 to 2 for acquittal.
So the government does have an uphill battle.
The defense says prosecutors are simply looking for a scapegoat.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in Los Angeles.
All nine people on board are a private jet that was traveling from Texas to the Bahamas
are dead after the plane crashed in South Florida yesterday.
Katie McCaffee from member station KUT has more.
Early reports suggest severe weather caused the plane to go from controlled flight to
a near vertical nosedive to the ground within minutes.
The plane was descending over 20,000 feet per minute before impact.
Aviation attorney Mike Slack said the weather conditions in Florida would not have been
suitable for any aircraft.
The most significant question this whole accident that I see is how and why the airplane ended
up where it did in dangerous proximity to the weather.
At a news conference, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said there were no reports of injuries
to people on the ground.
The investigation into the crash is ongoing.
For NPR News, I'm Katie McCaffee in Austin.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Japan's online service company, GMO Internet Group, is apologizing for security breaches
from cyber attacks and has promised to compensate victims.
The company's CEO and other executives bowed deeply at a press conference today in Tokyo
after confirming that hackers got into its onomay.com desktop cloud service affecting
dozens of security firms and other businesses.
GMO offers Internet services for cybersecurity, marketing, AI, robotics, and infrastructure
systems.
Lindsay Clancy will be back in a Massachusetts courtroom today for a hearing that could determine
if she will face another trial for the deaths of her children.
Deborah Becker from member station WBUR has more.
Prosecutors say although the first case ended in a mistrial, they should be allowed to continue
to "pursue justice" for the three Clancy children.
Criminal defense attorney Keith Halpern, who is not involved in the case, expects another
trial.
I don't think there was ever any question that they were going to retry this case in
one form or another.
The defense argues the mistrial was a mistake, and the judge should have further investigated
claims that one juror wouldn't follow the law.
The defense is not disputed that Clancy killed her children, but said she was experiencing
severe psychosis.
For NPR News, I'm Deborah Becker in Boston.
In world financial markets, Asian markets closed in mixed territory.
The Nikkei, the main market in Japan down three-tenths of a percent.
The Hang Seng and Hong Kong up four-tenths of a percent.
U.S. futures contracts are trading higher.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Trump rallies in Dubuque, Iowa, urging Republican votes and portraying Democrats as dangerous
Retrial begins in Los Angeles for Jonathan Rinderkinesh, accused of starting the Lachman fire
Private jet with nine aboard from Texas to Bahamas crashes in South Florida, killing all
Japan's GMO Internet Group apologizes for cyberattack breaches and promises victim compensation
Lindsay Clancy hearing in Massachusetts could determine whether she faces retrial for children's deaths
Asian markets close mixed; Nikkei falls while Hang Seng rises, U.S. futures trade higher
